segs.text: Module four, objective three. Creatinine clearance and what it means. The glomerular filtration rate, G F R, tells you how well a patient's kidneys are working. It is measured with a substance eliminated primarily by filtration only, one that is neither reabsorbed nor secreted. Inulin is almost completely filtered, so it is the better marker, but it is not native to the body: it has to be given, and the testing is more involved. Creatinine comes from the breakdown of muscle and is already in the blood, so creatinine clearance, C r C l, is the common clinical estimate of G F R. Creatinine is also secreted, which is why C r C l estimates G F R rather than measuring it.

card.m: GFR marker: filtered only, not reabsorbed, not secreted
inulin: almost completely filtered, must be given
creatinine: from muscle, already in the blood
CrCl estimates GFR: creatinine is also secreted

segs.text: C r C l is calculated with the Cockcroft-Gault equation, and one hundred twenty to one hundred thirty milliliters per minute is considered normal. C r C l equals one hundred forty minus age, times I B W, divided by seventy two times S C r, times zero point eight five if female. Age is in years, I B W is ideal body weight in kilograms, and S C r is serum creatinine in milligrams per deciliter. An older patient gets a lower estimate, because one hundred forty minus age gets smaller. A higher serum creatinine sits in the bottom of the fraction, so it also lowers the estimate. The zero point eight five factor rests on the assumption that women are smaller and less muscular than men.

card.m: CrCl = {{frac:(140 − age) × IBW|72 × S<sub>Cr</sub>}}   (× 0.85 if female)
age in years, IBW in kg, S<sub>Cr</sub> in mg/dL

segs.text: Ideal body weight, in kilograms, is calculated from sex and height. For a male, I B W equals fifty plus two point three times the inches over five feet. For a female, I B W equals forty five point five plus two point three times the inches over five feet. The inches over five feet are the height in inches minus sixty. Neither the I B W lines nor Cockcroft-Gault are on the equation sheet. The units do not cancel, since the algebra gives kilograms divided by milligrams per deciliter. She said, I also want you to recognize that the units of creatinine clearance should be in milliliters per minute So don't give me kilograms per milligram per deciliter.

card.m: inches over 5 ft = height in inches − 60

segs.text: When the height is given in centimeters, it is converted first. Height in inches equals height in centimeters divided by two point five four, because one inch is two point five four centimeters. A decimal height is read as written: sixty four point five inches is sixty four point five inches, not sixty four inches plus another five.

Her slide example. Estimate, using the ideal body weight, the C r C l of a forty five year old female who weighs sixty one kilograms, has a serum creatinine of one point one milligrams per deciliter, and is one hundred sixty five centimeters tall. First the height: one hundred sixty five centimeters divided by two point five four is sixty four point nine six inches, which she rounds to sixty five inches. The inches over five feet are sixty five minus sixty, which is five inches. She is female, so I B W is forty five point five plus two point three times five. That is forty five point five plus eleven point five, which is fifty seven kilograms. The sixty one kilogram actual weight is not used.

card.m: female, 45 yr, 61 kg, S<sub>Cr</sub> = 1.1 mg/dL, 165 cm

segs.text: Now Cockcroft-Gault. The top of the fraction is one hundred forty minus forty five, which is ninety five, times fifty seven kilograms, giving five thousand four hundred fifteen. The bottom is seventy two times one point one milligrams per deciliter, which is seventy nine point two. Five thousand four hundred fifteen divided by seventy nine point two is sixty eight point three seven. She is female, so that is multiplied by zero point eight five, which gives fifty eight point one milliliters per minute.

What the number means. Fifty eight point one milliliters per minute is below the normal one hundred twenty to one hundred thirty, so her renal function is reduced. A low C r C l means a drug eliminated by the kidney is excreted more slowly and may accumulate, so depending on the drug, its dose may need adjusting. In the same way, a C r C l of thirty milliliters per minute means a renally eliminated drug will be excreted more slowly and may accumulate. C r C l describes the patient's kidneys, not a particular drug. A drug's renal clearance, worked out in objective five from the fraction of the dose excreted unchanged, is a different number, and confusing the two is a trap she names herself.

card.m: low CrCl → slower excretion, accumulation, dose adjustment
Cl<sub>R</sub>: one drug, from f<sub>e</sub>   ✗ confusing the two

segs.text: How she tests it. A one patient vignette gives age, sex, height, actual body weight and serum creatinine, with the answer in milliliters per minute. The height usually arrives in centimeters, so the conversion is part of the question, and the actual weight is there to be left alone. Sex decides two things: which I B W constant is used, fifty or forty five point five, and whether the zero point eight five factor applies. When she worked this example, answers of one hundred four and fifty four milliliters per minute came back, and she said fifty four meant something had been done wrong.

card.m: given: age, sex, height, actual weight, S<sub>Cr</sub>
cm → inches; actual weight not used
